claim: k3s on the default SQLite datastore has no managed database driver, so its /db/ HTTP routes (used by the etcd-snapshot CLI) answer 'etcd datastore disabled'; k3s etcd-snapshot cannot back up a SQLite server
Lab: on k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 with SQLite, `k3s etcd-snapshot save` exits 1 with 'etcd datastore disabled' (H1 PASS)
k3s docs: no special commands are needed for SQLite; back up by copying /var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/db/ and restore its contents plus the token
k3s docs: the server token file must be backed up and restored (or passed as --token); without the same token the backup is unusable because the token encrypts confidential data in the datastore
A SQLite k3s server converts to embedded etcd in place by restarting with --cluster-init; the code copies every /registry/ key from kine into etcd and renames state.db to state.db.migrated
Lab: --cluster-init conversion of a restored SQLite box migrated 409 keys in about 15 s, left state.db.migrated, and all demo objects survived (H3 PASS)

k3s v1.37.2+k3s1 pins kine v0.17.1, whose SQLite driver opens the datastore in WAL mode (_journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL), so a plain file copy of state.db alone while k3s runs is not a consistent backup; use the SQLite online-backup API or stop k3s
kine v0.17.1 registers a 'litestream' driver that disables WAL checkpointing and startup VACUUM so Litestream can replicate the k3s SQLite datastore continuously

Lab: an online `sqlite3 .backup` of state.db (integrity_check ok) plus token, node password and a restic snapshot of /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage restored onto a second, freshly installed VM; the ConfigMap, the encrypted Secret and the PVC marker all came back (H2 PASS)

Lab: immediately after a restore the Node shows Ready and the Pod Running because that status comes from the restored datastore; `kubectl exec` failed ('container not found' / 'pod does not exist') until the kubelet re-created the container, so a restore health gate must not trust restored status
k3s scheduled etcd snapshots are on by default at 00:00 and 12:00 with 5 kept per server; on-demand snapshots have no retention and must be pruned manually
Restoring an etcd snapshot to a different host requires passing the original server token (--token), because it decrypts the bootstrap data inside the snapshot

k3s etcd snapshots contain the whole datastore plus CA certificates and private keys; anyone with the file can read unencrypted resources, and with the token also encrypted resources and CA keys; restoring an attacker-supplied snapshot gives them the cluster
Lab: both the SQLite backup and the etcd snapshot contain the test ConfigMap value in plaintext; the Secret value is not in plaintext when k3s runs with --secrets-encryption
k3s may restore a snapshot on the same or a higher patch/minor version within the Kubernetes skew policy, but not from an older version that could not be upgraded from directly
k3s rollback to an earlier minor needs a datastore snapshot taken on that minor (binary downgrade plus restore); for SQLite the rollback is replacing the .db file with the pre-upgrade copy

Lab: an etcd snapshot plus the token restored onto a wiped VM with --cluster-reset --cluster-reset-restore-path, then restic restored the app volume; objects and PVC data verified, about 13 s to API-ready on a tiny dataset (H4 PASS)
Lab (indicative, VM virtio disk, whole-disk counter, 10 min idle, one pod): about 19 MiB written on SQLite vs about 166 MiB on embedded etcd, roughly 8.7x; etcd data dir 142 MiB vs SQLite 13 MiB

k3s's bundled local-path provisioner (v0.0.37) uses defaultVolumeType 'local' and reclaimPolicy Delete; lab PVs are 'local' volumes with nodeAffinity to the node name, so deleting a PVC deletes app data and a restore must keep the node name
Velero 1.18 File System Backup is 'beta quality', does not support hostPath volumes (local volumes are supported), and can only back up volumes mounted by a running pod

If the velero-repo-credentials Secret does not exist, Velero creates it with the hard-coded repository password 'static-passw0rd'; one common key is used for all repositories, so anyone with storage access can decrypt unless the operator pre-creates the Secret
Velero's restic data path is deprecated (since v1.15); Kopia is the uploader going forward
restic encrypts with AES-256-CTR and authenticates with Poly1305-AES; a repository can hold multiple keys that each open it; license BSD-2-Clause
restic append-only mode (served by rest-server or rclone) stops a compromised client from deleting backups; forget/prune need full access and should run from a separate, well-secured client
restic latest release v0.19.1 (2026-07-05); Debian 13 apt ships restic 0.18.0 (lab)

restic index memory grows with repository size: issue #1988 'reduce index memory usage' open since 2018; #3374 reports a 1 GB Raspberry Pi 3 running out of memory after a 3 TB backup was added to the same repository
Kopia: Apache-2.0; default encryption AES256-GCM-HMAC-SHA256; default password key derivation scrypt-65536-8-1
Kopia allows one password per repository and has no access control when a repository is shared
Kopia supports optional Reed-Solomon error correction since v0.12
borg: 1.4.5 is the stable line (2026-07-18); borg 2 is still beta with breaking changes and no beta-to-beta upgrade path; borg 1.x reaches remote repositories over SSH; licence is BSD 3-clause
Longhorn 1.13: backups created from encrypted volumes are encrypted; volume encryption uses dm_crypt/LUKS with the key held in a Kubernetes Secret (so unencrypted volumes give unencrypted backups)
OpenZFS `zfs send -w` (raw) sends encrypted datasets as stored, so a backup can be received on an untrusted machine that cannot read or undetectably alter it
k8up v2.16.1 is an Apache-2.0 Kubernetes backup operator built on restic, with a pod annotation (k8up.io/backupcommand) for application-aware dumps
VolSync v0.17.0 (used by the founder's cluster) is AGPL-3.0 and replicates PVCs with rsync, rclone or restic movers
Litestream is Apache-2.0, latest v0.5.18 (2026-11-03)
HA Supervisor apps declare a backup mode: HOT (default; optional backup_pre/backup_post commands run inside the container) or COLD (Supervisor stops the app during backup and restarts it)
HA Supervisor tells HA Core over the websocket when a backup begins and ends (BACKUP_START/BACKUP_END) and can exclude the recorder database files
SecureTar (HA backup format) v3 = XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretstream with Argon2id and per-file BLAKE2b subkeys (default); v2 = AES-128-CBC with 100 SHA-256 rounds (legacy); outer archive is a plain tar

HA docs: backups are encrypted by default; the emergency-kit key is required to restore; a backup can be restored during onboarding on a different device type, e.g. from a Raspberry Pi to another device
HA Cloud stores one backup (the latest) up to 5 GB, always encrypted
umbreld backs up hourly; a Kopia repository may only be created on a network share or an external drive; retention keep-latest 10, hourly 24, daily 7, weekly 4, monthly 12, annual 0
umbreld stores as Kopia password the first 16 hex characters (64 bits) of SHA-256(user password), while the code comment says 128 bits; Kopia then applies scrypt

umbreld snapshots the live data directory while apps keep running; only its own umbrel.db is materialised as a standalone SQLite snapshot checked with quick_check (live db/WAL files ignored), and VMs are pivoted to overlays; no app stop or app hook was found in the backup path
umbreld honours per-app backupIgnore paths from the app manifest and lets users exclude whole apps
umbreld exposes restoreBackup as a procedure callable when no user exists yet, i.e. restore during onboarding of a fresh box
umbrelOS 2.0.1 (stable) pins Kopia 0.19.0; 2.1.0-beta.1 and master pin Kopia 0.23.1 (corrects context/03, which lists 0.23.1 for the current release)

Umbrel issue #2207: Kopia's unbounded cache exhausted the SD card's inodes on a Pi 4 and backups failed silently for about 22 hours while the dashboard looked healthy; closed 2026-08-22; current code caps the cache on filesystems with 5 million inodes or fewer
Umbrel support page (updated 2026-10-02): hourly encrypted backups to another Umbrel, a NAS or USB; GFS retention; destination needs twice the backup size; Umbrel Private Cloud 'coming soon'

Umbrel forum (2026-09-23): a 100 GB restore from an SMB share during onboarding of a clean 2.0 install hung on the folder browser; restoring later from Settings finished but restored nothing; no reply
Olares backup-server uses a restic SDK; app-level backup is cooperative (it calls the app's own {app}/backup/start, status, result HTTP endpoints) and is hardwired to the Wise app host
HA forum (2025-07): after a storm a user rebuilt HAOS but could not restore any backup because the encryption key was lost with the old install; they rebuilt by hand (about 3 days)
TrueNAS forum (2024-07): a SCALE user's k3s datastore failed with 'Compact failed ... database disk image is malformed' (SQLite wording); no resolution posted
Founder Blueprint targets: Core/identity RPO <=1 h, RTO <=4 h on a prepared spare; knowledge RPO <=24 h; a backup counts as verified only after a restore drill; keys held outside the cluster

Lab timings on a tiny dataset (2 vCPU arm64 VMs): online SQLite+restic backup 4.0 s; SQLite restore to API-ready 5.8 s; etcd snapshot restore to API-ready 13.0 s; times scale with data size and link speed
k3s latest stable releases on 2026-11-10: v1.37.2+k3s1 and v1.36.6+k3s1 (2026-11-03)

The founder's cluster already runs a verified-restore pattern: each PostgreSQL dump is encrypted, uploaded, downloaded again, integrity-checked and restored into a scratch database before a 'verified' marker is written; the cluster-recovery export is verified by decrypt/equality only, not replay
Velero supports pre/post backup hooks declared as pod annotations (pre.hook.backup.velero.io/container, /command, /on-error, /timeout), with an fsfreeze example for crash-consistent volume backups
